evidence: Receiving DO2 steps from 11.76 mg/L (48.0 h) to 6.69 mg/L (48.2 h) and stays at 6.36 mg/L at 52.0 h, a sustained ~5 mg/L regime shift with no recovery
Source batches 1-3 at 48-52 h show DO2 of 10.5-11.3 mg/L at the same product stage, indicating receiving-vessel oxygen imbalance
Receiving P assay trajectory (0 -> 0.0013 -> 1.09 -> 3.11 g/L) matches source batches, which peak near 8 g/L at 72-76 h during highest oxygen demand
DO2 minimum constraint is 2.0 mg/L; current margin is only ~4.4 mg/L entering the highest-demand production window
Allowed combined action is bounded: feed 0.8x, air 1.15x, retaining production and product mass unlike stop
args.rationale: The receiving fermenter shows an abrupt, sustained ~5 mg/L DO2 drop at 48.2 h (11.8 to ~6.4 mg/L) that has not recovered over 4 hours, unlike all three source batches which held ~10.5-11.3 mg/L at the same age. Product is on a source-like trajectory (3.11 g/L at 48 h) and source history shows oxygen demand peaks in the 52-72 h window. DO2 is above the 2.0 mg/L minimum but margin is thin heading into the highest-demand phase. The combined intervention (feed 0.8x, air 1.15x) is bounded and reversible: it reduces oxygen demand while increasing oxygen supply, protecting the constraint without stopping production (stop would yield zero counted production and discard accumulated product mass) and without the excessive throttling of strong_feed_reduction.
args.uncertainty: The DO2 plateau at ~6.4 mg/L may be a stable new equilibrium rather than a deteriorating trend, in which case 'keep' would suffice; hidden receiving parameters (kLa, feed composition, organism state) are unobservable, so the 1.15x air ceiling may not fully restore margin if demand keeps rising; delayed assay clocks mean the true current product level is up to 4 h stale.
